newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch- June 2.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch- June 2.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Monday:

** Indian shares are seen quiet this week as participants seek clues on market direction amid uncertainity about the timing of a hike in government-set oil prices, analysts and dealers said at the weekend.
But some traders said a technical correction in share prices late last week coupled with renewed fund buying could see the market moving higher.
** The decision-making Steering Committee of India's ruling United Front will meet on June 8 to reach a consensus on increasing oil prices, Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said on Saturday.
"There are four or five options to tackle the oil pool deficit," Gujral told reporters before leaving for New Delhi after a day-long visit to Bombay.
He said the committee will consider these options and would have to arrive at a consensus decision at their June 8 meeting.
** Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M) is entering into a 50:50 joint venture with the $8 billion-Case of the US for manufacturing high horse power tractors, the Economic Times daily reports.
Although discussions have reached an advanced stage, M&M is yet to decide on the exact location of the manufacturing facility for the new tractor project, the paper says.
The joint venture has fixed an initial investment of 3.0 billion rupees for the first two years, the paper reports.
** Escorts and Blue Star are due to announce their annual results for the year ending March 31, 1997 later on Monday.
** The Indian rupee opened unchanged at 35.78/79 on Monday, dealers said.
The dollar is seen easing as little dollar demand seen on the first working day of the new month, they said.
